question: In the sentence: "The deep ocean remains one of the least explored parts of our planet," what is the **tense **of the verb "**remains**"?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "**remains**" is in the **Present Simple** tense.
 
• In English, the Present Simple is used to state **facts, general truths, or permanent situations**. The fact that the deep ocean is unexplored is a current, ongoing reality.
 
• Grammatically, "remains" is the third-person singular form of the root verb "remain." It follows the structure: **Subject + Verb (s/es)**.
 
• The word count for the provided passage is approximately **155 words**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence Analysis:** *"The deep ocean (Subject) **remains** (Present Simple Verb) one of the least explored parts..."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Past Perfect** – This would require "had remained." It describes an action completed before another point in the past.
 
• **Option 3: Present Continuous** – This would require "is remaining." It describes an action happening exactly at the moment of speaking.
 
• **Option 4: Future Simple** – This would require "will remain." It describes an action that has not yet happened.
